To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Galileo E5a mass market receiver should be designed with E1/E5 dual-frequency capability, and the baseband architecture should be common with the E1 channel and the E5a channel.
E5a/E1 combination is the best dual-frequency option, a flexible dual-frequency baseband is the best implementation approach.
the E1/E5 dual frequency option is the best solution for a Galileo receiver, and a common dual-frequency architecture is a suitable solution for this type of receiver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal frequency combination for a mass market Galileo receiver.
the impact of dual frequencies on Galileo mass market baseband algorithms and their implementation.

the following issues: the impact of dual-frequency on Galileo mass market baseband algorithms and implementation issues of a Galileo dual-frequency baseband; the analysis results indicate that E1/E5 combination is the best option and a common dual-frequency architecture with flexible channels is the best implementation approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E1/E5 combination is the optimal solution for a Galileo baseband.
a Galileo E5a receiver with an E1 channel would be the optimal solution for a dual frequency mass market receiver.
E1/E5b combination would be the optimal dual-frequency option for a Galilee mass market receiver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E1/E5b combination is the optimal choice for the Galileo mass market baseband.
the E1/E5b combination is a better option than E1/E5e, E1/E5f and E1/E5q.
a mass market Galileo E1 and E5a receiver can be implemented with a dual frequency baseband architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal dual-frequency option is not the same as the optimal single-frequency option.
the optimal frequency combination for Galilee is not E1/E5b but rather E1/E5al.
